channel.title: bench.log
channel.description: A running log of local AI work on ordinary hardware: RTX 5070 Ti benchmarks, ComfyUI and Flux LoRA workflows, on-prem RAG deployments. Real configs and measured numbers, written as the work happens.

item.title: I bought the whole server, and now I get to do nothing about it for a week
item.description: Every part for the third local AI node is bought and none of it has arrived. Why the RTX 3090 leaving my desktop is the real cost, and the rules I'm setting before I film the assembly.

item.title: I'm building a 40 GB AI server out of 2014 server parts, and the GPUs are the boring half
item.description: Dual Xeon E5-2620 v3, Supermicro X10DRi-T4+, 112 GB DDR4, 40 GB pooled VRAM. Why the GPUs are the least interesting decision in the build.

item.title: My illustration model rendered photographs, and turning the dial did nothing
item.description: A trained Flux style LoRA returned photoreal images on scene pages at every strength setting. The fix was a prompt clause, not a weight.

item.title: Why a tax advisor's Excel habit broke my RAG pipeline
item.description: Six bugs from an on-prem RAG pilot (FastAPI, ChromaDB, Ollama Qwen 2.5 14B).

item.title: Cleaning up 30 dead HTML files taught me more about deploys than the deploy did
item.description: Replacing manual drag-and-drop Netlify deploys with GitHub continuous deployment — and what consolidating the source of truth turned up: 30 dead HTML files and a Fraktur font with unintended associations in Germany.

item.title: A client asked if I could train a custom model on their images. I didn't know yet.
item.description: Scoping on-prem LoRA fine-tuning as a real client offering: why it isn't a bolt-on feature, and why per-image pricing is the wrong model for something that doesn't scale like inference.
